grisalho-natural: Natural gray, a soft medium silver-gray made of a natural mix of pure white, light gray and a few remaining darker ash-brown strands, about three quarters white overall. Cool-neutral tone with no yellow, brass or dyed look. Evenly distributed from roots to ends, slightly darker and denser underneath and at the nape, lighter and more silvery at the front hairline and temples. Individually visible multi-tonal strands and a soft satin shine, the realistic look of naturally grown-out gray hair.
transicao-grisalha: Gray blending transition: natural silver-gray roots melting seamlessly into a softened light ash-brown through the mid-lengths and ends, with fine woven silver and pale ash-blonde highlights plus a few soft cool lowlights threaded throughout, so there is no demarcation line between the gray regrowth and the previous color. Cool, smoky, multi-tonal result with diffused transitions, brighter silver at the part line and face-framing pieces. Natural strand-by-strand variation and a soft healthy shine, a realistic professional gray-blending service.
sal-e-pimenta: Salt and pepper, a natural dark brown-black level 2-3 base with fine, evenly scattered pure white and silver strands woven throughout, roughly half dark and half white, giving a speckled, high-contrast gray effect from roots to ends. Slightly more white at the temples, front hairline and crown, more dark strands underneath and at the nape. Cool-neutral, no yellow or dyed-brown cast, no chunky stripes or sections. Individually distinguishable white and dark strands with a soft natural shine, a realistic naturally graying look.
prateado: Bright silver, a luminous light silver-gray around level 9 with a clean, cool pearl-ash tone and zero yellow: the even, toned silver of fully embraced gray hair. Consistent from roots to ends, with soft pewter-gray shadows in the depth of the hair and underneath, and brilliant white-silver reflections on the surface where light hits. Subtle natural variation between whiter and grayer strands, never a flat wig color, and a silky reflective shine, a realistic professional silver-toner result.
branco-natural: Natural white, a clean bright snow-white like fully white natural hair, with a neutral-cool tone and no yellow, cream or brassy cast. Even from roots to ends, with very faint soft silver-gray shadows in the depth of the hair and underneath, and luminous pure-white highlights on the surface. Fine, translucent, individually visible white strands with gentle natural variation and a soft silky shine, never icy blue, chalky or matte, a realistic healthy white-hair result.
luzes-disfarca-brancos: Gray-camouflage highlights: many fine, criss-crossed herringbone-style highlights in light ash and beige blonde, level 8-9, woven densely through a medium ash-brown, naturally graying base, so the white strands blend in and read as soft blonde dimension. Concentrated at the part line, crown and face-framing pieces, softly diffused at the roots so regrowth is invisible. Cool-neutral beige-ash result with no orange or brassiness, multi-tonal blended strands and a natural shine, a realistic professional blending service.
grisalho-com-lowlights: Silver gray with lowlights: a bright natural silver-gray base enriched with fine woven lowlights in soft charcoal and cool ash-brown, around level 5-6, spread evenly through the mid-lengths and ends and a little underneath, adding depth and contrast. The silver stays dominant, especially at the roots, part line and around the face, while the darker ribbons create dimension and movement. Cool tones only with no warmth or brass, seamlessly blended placement and a soft satin shine, a realistic professional lowlight result.
mecha-branca-frontal: Bold white front streak: two crisp face-framing sections at the front hairline, one on each side of the part and about two fingers wide, lifted from roots to ends to a clean bright white-silver with no yellow, while the rest of the hair keeps its current color exactly as it is. High-contrast, cleanly placed panels like the iconic skunk-stripe money piece, with sharp but natural edges. Individual white strands stay visible and shiny, a realistic professional bleach-and-toner result.
grisalho-chumbo: Pewter gray, a deep natural steel gray around level 6: a dense mix of charcoal and medium slate-gray strands with a few silver-white strands, cool and smoky with no brown, blue or yellow cast. Even from roots to ends, darker and denser underneath and at the nape, slightly lighter steel-gray on the surface where light hits. Natural strand-to-strand variation and a soft satin finish, not metallic or chrome, the realistic look of naturally dark gray hair.
grisalho-greige: Greige, a soft blend of light silver-gray and creamy beige blonde around level 8-9: a warm-neutral gray with gentle beige undertones, softer and warmer than icy silver, with no yellow brass and no harsh ash. Hand-painted balayage-style placement, slightly smokier gray-taupe at the roots melting seamlessly into lighter beige-silver mid-lengths and ends, with brighter pieces around the face. Multi-tonal blended strands and a satiny natural shine, a realistic professional greige toning result.
ombre-prateado: Silver ombré, a horizontal gradient from deep natural dark brown roots, level 3-4, melting through a smoky ash-gray transition at the mid-lengths into bright silver-white ends. The dark zone covers roughly the upper third of the hair, the blend is soft and seamless with no harsh line, and the silver is cool and clean with no yellow or brass. Multi-tonal strands within each zone and a healthy shine, a realistic professional bleach-and-silver-toner result.
prata-perolado: Pearl silver, a very light silver-white around level 9-10 with an iridescent pearl reflect: a cool silver base with delicate shimmering hints of lilac, soft pink and champagne that appear as the light moves, never reading as pink or lavender hair. Even from roots to ends, with soft dove-gray shadows underneath and luminous mother-of-pearl highlights on the surface. Fine multi-tonal strand variation and a high satin shine, a realistic professional pearl-silver toner result.
prateado-raiz-esfumada: Silver with a shadow root: bright cool silver-gray, level 9, through the mid-lengths and ends, with a soft smoky charcoal-ash shadow root covering the first few centimeters from the scalp that diffuses seamlessly into the silver with no visible line. Clean silver with zero yellow, gentle pewter shadows underneath and luminous white-silver reflections on the surface. Natural strand-to-strand variation and a smooth satin shine, a realistic professional root-smudge and silver-toner result.
